newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- DEC 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- DEC 31.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Questions about the maritime tragedy that has left 20 crewmembers of the "Dystos" dead or missing and presumed dead continue to go unanswered. The prime minister has asked the merchant marine ministry to fully examine the tragedy.
--The finance ministry will attempt to cover its lending needs by a plethora of T-bill and bond issues in January.

--All eyes have turned towards the meeting between conservative opposition leader Miltiades Evert, his lieutenant Ioannis Varvitsiotis and leadership contender George Souflias, probably on Saturday, which will determine the atmosphere for the party's course to its congress.

--An admission of disorganisation came from the merchant marine ministry yesterday when minister Stavros Soumakis suspended five officers pending an investigation into negligence over the "Dystos" tragedy.
--The purchase of state-of-the-art helicopters that would assist in sea search and rescue operations has been delayed eight years by vested interests, diplomatic pressures and kickbacks.
--A European Commission report shows Greece to have 50 more shipping accidents that Britain and 25 more than Denmark.
--A bomb planted by a Greek organisation in the heart of Athens at the Peruvian embassy to express solidarity with the Tupac Amaru guerrillas slightly injured a passerby.
--Greece sees out the old year with pain and grief, a bomb for Peru and hope for a better New Year.
--Reports say the victims of the Dystos may have been alive for some three hours, trapped in the capsized ship.
--Two crucial mistakes in the ministry's Operations Room were fatal for the unlucky Dystos and delayed rescue efforts for nine hours.
--The fisherman who found the lone survivor of the Dystos says he had no idea there had been an accident. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
